mainTopic: חציצה in טבילה: mud, food, scabs, the eyes, posture and knotted hair
overview: This amud is a list of rulings about חציצה, anything that comes between a woman's body and the water of the מקוה. It opens by finishing a ruling that a woman should not immerse at a muddy port, because mud may have stuck to her and then fallen off on the way out. אבוה דשמואל put this concern into practice by spreading mats on the muddy riverbed for his daughters. רב then rules that a woman who handled food right before immersing has an invalid טבילה, for the same reason. Next come rulings about things on the body: bloodletting scabs block only after three days, and eye discharge blocks only once it is dry. Eye makeup blocks only when it sits on the outside of the eye. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש teach that the eyes and body must be held in a natural, relaxed way, not squeezed shut or forced open. ריש לקיש's rule is supported by a משנה about how people stand for a צרעת inspection. The amud ends with רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that even one knotted hair is a חציצה, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do not immerse at a muddy port
steps.stepSummary: The ruling ends: a woman should not immerse at a port. Mud may have blocked the water and then fallen off as she walked out.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...in a port. Even though right now there is no mud on her, we say it may have fallen off while she was walking out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that a woman should not do her טבילה at a port, where the ground is very muddy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that mud stuck to her body during the טבילה and caused a חציצה. Checking her afterward does not help, because the mud could have dropped off on the way out. Since we cannot be sure the water reached her whole body, she should not immerse there.

keyTerms.meaning: A port, the shore where boats are pulled up. It is a very muddy place.
Right now there is nothing there
It fell off while she was walking
Something that blocks the water from touching the body during טבילה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is solved if she checks herself after the טבילה and finds no mud. The whole point is that a clean body afterward proves nothing, because the mud could have fallen off on the way out.

phrases.english: in a port,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started before this section: a woman should not immerse in a port.

phrases.english: even though now there is nothing [on her] —
say that it fell off while she was walking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּהַשְׁתָּא לֵיכָּא אֵימַר בְּרִדְיוֹנֵי נְפַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling that began earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman should not immerse at a muddy port. Mud may have blocked the water and then fallen off, so seeing no mud afterward does not prove the טבילה was valid.

steps.title: How שמואל's father protected his daughters' immersion
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל made מקואות for his daughters in ניסן, and in תשרי he put mats on the riverbed so they would not step in mud.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father made ritual baths for his daughters in the days of ניסן, and mats in the days of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of practical behavior that fits the worry about mud and חציצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תשרי the river was low and its bottom was muddy, so he spread mats for his daughters to stand on. That kept mud off their bodies, the same concern as the port ruling. The text here gives no reason for the ניסן מקואות. Elsewhere the גמרא ties that practice to the river being swollen with rainwater, which is a different concern from mud.

keyTerms.meaning: Mats made of reeds or rushes
The spring month, when rivers are full
The autumn month, when rivers are low

phrases.english: Shmuel's father made for his daughters
ritual baths in the days of Nisan,
and mats in the days of Tishrei.
phrases.notes: He spread the mats on the muddy river bottom so the girls would not stand in mud while immersing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mats in תשרי show the mud concern from step 1 being put into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is proper to take practical steps to keep mud off the body during טבילה.

steps.title: Handling food right before immersing makes the immersion invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב: if a woman fed her son cooked food and then immersed, her טבילה does not count. Food may have stuck to her and fallen off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: If she gave a cooked dish to her son, then immersed and came up, the immersion does not count for her. Even though now nothing is on her, we say it fell off while she was walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case that uses the exact same reasoning as the port: food in place of mud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bits of food may have stuck to her hands from handling the dish and blocked the water. Finding no food on her afterward does not help, since it could have dropped off on the way out. Here רב goes further and says the טבילה actually does not count, not only that she should avoid doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: It did not count for her, so the טבילה is invalid

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the source for being careful not to handle sticky food right before טבילה.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
[If] she gave a cooked dish to her son,
and she immersed and came up —
the immersion does not count for her,
even though now there is nothing [on her],
say that it fell off while she was walking.
phrases.notes: Same words as in step 1, but now 'it' means bits of food instead of mud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב נָתְנָה תַּבְשִׁיל לִבְנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'it may have fallen off' reasoning from step 1 to food residue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who handled cooked food and then immersed has an invalid טבילה, because food may have blocked the water and then fallen off.

steps.title: Bloodletting cuts block only after three days
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא: bloodletting cuts do not block the water for the first three days. After that, once a hard scab forms, they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said: These bloodletting cuts do not block until three days. From then on, they do block.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new חציצה ruling about the scab that forms on a bloodletting cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first three days the wound is still soft, so it does not count as a block. After three days the scab hardens and water cannot reach the skin under it, so it becomes a חציצה. The deciding factor is time, which tells us how hard the scab is.

keyTerms.meaning: Cuts or marks left from bloodletting
They block, meaning they count as a חציצה

steps.whatToRemember: A חציצה is anything that keeps water from the body. Mud and food are a worry even after they are gone, because they may have been there during the טבילה. A bloodletting scab blocks only once it has hardened, after three days.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this backward. The fresh cut, in the first three days, is the one that does NOT block. The older, hardened scab is the one that does.

phrases.english: Rami bar Abba said:
these bloodletting cuts,
until three days — they do not block,
from then on — they block.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא הָנֵי רִבְדֵי דְּכוּסִילְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new kind of חציצה: something on the body itself rather than dirt from outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodletting cuts do not count as a חציצה for the first three days. After that they do.

steps.title: Eye discharge: moist does not block, dry does
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא rules that moist eye discharge is not a חציצה, but dry discharge is. It counts as dry once it starts turning yellow.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא said: Discharge in the eye, if it is moist, does not block the water. If it is dry, it blocks. When is it called dry? From when it starts to turn yellow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ruling to its list of things that might block the water during טבילה, this time about discharge in the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moist discharge is soft, so the water can reach through it or it washes away. Dry discharge has hardened and sits on the body like a separate thing, so it blocks. The turning-yellow sign gives a clear, practical line for when it counts as dry.

keyTerms.meaning: Discharge or crust that collects in the eye
Blocks the water from reaching the body (makes a חציצה)

phrases.english: Mar Ukva said:
Discharge that is in the eye:
if moist, it does not block;
if dry, it blocks.
When is it called dry?
From the time it begins to turn yellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like רמי בר אבא's ruling on bloodletting scabs, this is another case where soft does not block and hardened does.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moist eye discharge is not a חציצה; dry discharge, from when it starts turning yellow, is a חציצה.

steps.title: Eye makeup inside the eye versus on the eyelid
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that כחול inside the eye does not block, but כחול on the outside of the eye does, unless the woman's eyes blink constantly.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Eye makeup inside the eye does not block. Eye makeup on top of the eye blocks. If her eyes were always blinking, even makeup on top of the eye does not block.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives another eye ruling, this time about כחול, the makeup women put on and around the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Makeup inside the eye is not counted as a block, but makeup sitting on the outside of the eye is. The exception: if her eyes blink all the time, the makeup does not stay put, so it is not treated as blocking.

keyTerms.meaning: Eye makeup, like eyeliner or eye shadow
On top of the eye, on the outside of the eye area

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Eye makeup that is inside the eye does not block,
but that which is on the outside of the eye blocks.
If her eyes were blinking,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עַל גַּבֵּי הָעַיִן אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.english: even on the outside of the eye it does not block.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the eye, moving from discharge to makeup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כחול inside the eye is not a חציצה; on the outside it is, unless her eyes blink constantly.

steps.title: Opening or squeezing the eyes too much ruins the immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if a woman opened her eyes very wide or shut them very tightly during טבילה, the טבילה does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If she opened her eyes too much, or shut her eyes too much, her טבילה does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן moves from things on the eye to how she holds her eyes during the dip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here nothing foreign is on her body. The problem is the posture itself: eyes squeezed shut or forced wide fold the skin around the eye, so the water cannot reach those spots.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
If she opened her eyes too much,
or shut her eyes too tightly,
her immersion does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from objects on the eye to the way the eyes are held.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eyes forced wide open or squeezed tightly shut make the טבילה invalid.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean her eyes must be open or closed. She should simply hold them in a normal, relaxed way.

steps.title: A woman immerses in her natural posture
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that a woman should immerse only in her natural way of standing, without squeezing her body together or spreading it unnaturally.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: A woman should immerse only in the natural way her body grows.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a related rule for the whole body: a woman immerses in her normal, natural posture. It fits with רבי יוחנן's rule about the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressing arms tightly to the sides or legs tightly together would hide skin from the water. But she also does not need to stretch everything wide open. The standard is the body's natural, relaxed position.

keyTerms.meaning: The way she naturally grows, her normal relaxed posture

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A woman should not immerse
except in the way she grows,
phrases.notes: He means her ordinary, relaxed stance: not squeezed together and not stretched out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the idea of 'not too much' from the eyes to the whole body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman must immerse in her natural posture.

steps.title: Support from how a person stands for a צרעת inspection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports ריש לקיש with a משנה in נגעים: a man is inspected standing like one hoeing or picking olives, and a woman like one weaving or nursing her son.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: A man is inspected looking like someone hoeing or harvesting olives. A woman is inspected looking like someone weaving, or like someone nursing her son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show where ריש לקיש's 'natural posture' idea comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a כהן inspects a mark of צרעת, the person stands in a normal working pose, not stretched open. Only what shows in that pose counts. In the same way, for טבילה, only the body in its natural pose needs to touch the water.

keyTerms.meaning: Hoeing the ground, legs slightly apart

steps.whatToRemember: For טבילה, the water must reach every part of the body that is exposed in a normal, relaxed posture. Squeezing (eyes, arms, legs) blocks the water, but she does not have to stretch beyond the natural.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: נגעים 2:4, about how a person stands while a כהן checks a mark of צרעת.

phrases.english: A man is seen as one who is hoeing
and harvesting olives;
a woman is seen as one who is weaving
and like one nursing her son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's rule that טבילה is done in the natural posture
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה נגעים 2:4: people are inspected for צרעת in natural working poses

steps.title: A single knotted hair blocks the immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that one hair tied in a knot is a חציצה and invalidates the טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: A single hair that is tied in a knot is a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling about barriers in טבילה: even one knotted hair counts as a חציצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps dealt with things on the eyes and how the woman stands. Now the focus moves to hair. A knot stops the water from reaching the hair inside it, so even one knotted hair is enough to block the טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Blocks, forms a barrier (חציצה) between the body and the water

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think only a big clump of hair blocks. Here even one single hair, if it is knotted, is a חציצה.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
A single hair tied in a knot is a barrier,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling to the series of rulings on what counts as a barrier during טבילה, now about hair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even one hair tied in a knot is a חציצה and invalidates the טבילה.
